stated: Reform UK will lift the income tax starting threshold to £20,000, which they state will take 7 million people out of income tax and save every worker almost £1,500 per year. The higher rate threshold will be raised to £70,000.

source.quote: Make Work Pay. Lift the Income Tax Start Point to £20,000 Per Year This frees up to 7 million people from paying Income Tax and saves every worker almost £1,500 per year. Basic Tax rate stays at 20%. The higher rate should begin at £70,000.

bearing_set.reason: Raising the income tax threshold to £20,000 directly increases take-home/disposable income for workers earning above the current threshold (~£12,570), with the stated saving of ~£1,500 per year constituting a material, non-negligible effect on real disposable income and ability to afford essentials.

The policy directly raises real net pay for workers — a core indicator of 'good work and fair pay' — and the removal of 7 million people from income tax particularly benefits lower-wage workers, bearing on in-work poverty.

Directly raises the income tax-free allowance from £12,570 to £20,000 and the higher-rate threshold to £70,000, materially increasing take-home pay for tens of millions of workers — a core O11 effect.

A cut of this scale (roughly £40–50bn in lost annual revenue at current taxpayer numbers) would materially widen the funding gap unless fully offset, concretely moving the debt-path sustainability indicator.

The personal allowance rise is broadly proportional in cash terms (same £1,486 for all earners above £20k), but the higher-rate threshold rise disproportionately benefits earners above £50,270, widening the income gap — a concrete distributional mechanism scored on O14.

membership_note: Three clear bearings: a tax-cut benefit (O11), a fiscal sustainability cost (O12), and a regressive distributional tilt from the higher-rate threshold change (O14). Effects on prices (O2) and aggregate growth (O13) are real but secondary to the dominant O11/O12/O14 mechanisms and would not earn independent non-negligible verdicts here.
